Dispatching to sub-commands

Zuguang Gu (guzuguang@suat-sz.edu.cn)

2026-11-24

Source: vignettes/sub_commands.Rmd
sub_commands.Rmd
## Warning: package 'knitr' was built under R version 4.6.1

A quick example

When a script gets complicated, it might be better to split it into several sub-scripts where each is focused on a specific task. Here sub_commands() supports to dispatch command-line options to sub-scripts.

The following code gives you a quick example of how the sub commands are set. In the function sub_commands(), the name of the sub-command, the sub-script and the description of the sub-command are organized as a 3-tuple.

The following code is put in the script called main.R (parent script) which contains dispatches of sub-commands.

library(argitect)

sub_commands(
    "sub1", "sub1.R", "Description of sub command 1.",
    "sub2", "sub2.R", "Description of sub command 2."
)

Code in sub1.R:

library(argitect)

argitect("foo=i", "Set value for foo.")

cat("foo is ", foo, "\n")

And code in sub2.R:

library(argitect)

argitect("bar=i", "Set value for bar")

cat("bar is ", bar, "\n")

Calling main.R with no argument prints the list of sub-commands it supports.

~\> Rscript main.R
Usage: Rscript foo.R [command] [options]

Commands:
  sub1    Description of sub command 1.
  sub2    Description of sub command 2.

When a sub-command is called, the corresponding R script is invoked. Here all command-line arguments after the sub command sub1 go to the correspond R script sub1.R. Internally, it actually executes Rscript sub1.R --help.

~\> Rscript main.R sub1 --help
Usage: Rscript foo.R sub1 [options]

Options:
  --foo, -f integer
    Set value for foo. 
  --help, -h
    Print help message and exit. 
  --version, -v
    Print version information and exit.

Options in sub1.R can be directly set after the sub-command, which internally equivalent to Rscript sub1.R --foo 10.

~\> Rscript main.R sub1 --foo 10
foo is 10

A shebang line can be added to the first line of the parent R script, then Rscript is not necessary to be explicitely called. Also .R suffix of the parent script can be removed to pretend it is a linux utility program.

#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
library(argitect)

sub_commands(
    "sub1", "sub1.R", "This is sub-command 1.",
    "sub2", "sub2.R", "This is sub-command 2."
)

Make sure main is executable.

./main sub1 --foo 1

If the directory of script main is put into PATH and all sub-command scripts are accessible from main, then

main sub1 --foo 1

The specification

Besides the 3-tuple specification demonstrated already, sub-commands can also be specified in 2-tuples, where the first element is the sub-script and the second element is the description of the sub-command. In this scenario, the basename of the sub-script removing .R/.r suffix is taken as the name of the sub-command.

sub_commands(
    "sub1.R", "This is sub-command 1.",
    "sub2.R", "This is sub-command 2."
)

With 3-tuple specification, names of the sub-commands can be self-defined.

sub_commands(
    "one", "sub1.R", "This is sub-command 1.",
    "two", "sub2.R", "This is sub-command 2."
)
Usage: Rscript foo.R [command] [options]

Commands:
  one    This is sub-command 1.
  two    This is sub-command 2.

As all parameters are specified as a long vector in sub_commands(), whether it is a 3-tuple format or a 2-tuple format is automatically determined.

Sections

A separator line (a name consisting only of -, =, +, # or %) starts a new section, just like in argitect(). The section title is the corresponding description. With the 3-tuple form:

sub_commands(
    "----", "----", "Section one",
    "sub1", "sub1.R", "This is sub-command 1.",

    "----", "----", "Section two",
    "sub2", "sub2.R", "This is sub-command 2."
)
Usage: Rscript foo.R [command] [options]

Section one
  sub1    This is sub-command 1.

Section two
  sub2    This is sub-command 2.

And with the 2-tuple form:

sub_commands(
    "----", "Section one",
    "sub1.R", "This is sub-command 1.",

    "----", "Section two",
    "sub2.R", "This is sub-command 2."
)
Usage: Rscript foo.R [command] [options]

Section one
  sub1    This is sub-command 1.

Section two
  sub2    This is sub-command 2.

Setting help head and foot

help_head adds text before the help message and help_foot adds text after the help message.

sub_commands(
    help_head = "This is the head of the help message.",

    "sub1", "sub1.R", "This is sub-command 1.",
    "sub2", "sub2.R", "This is sub-command 2.",

    help_foot = "This is the foot of the help message."
)
This is the head of the help message.

Usage: Rscript foo.R [command] [options]

Commands:
  sub1    This is sub-command 1.
  sub2    This is sub-command 2.

This is the foot of the help message.

Template

A single string is treated as a template, where each command is marked by the template_tag (default <CODE>). The code part can be either script.R (the command name is derived from the file name) or command=script.R:

sub_commands(
"This is the head of the help message.

Usage: Rscript main.R [command] [options]

Commands:
  <sub1.R> This is sub-command 1.
  <sub2=sub2.R> This is sub-command 2.

This is the foot of the help message.
")
This is the head of the help message. 
 
Usage: Rscript main.R [command] [options] 
 
Commands: 
  sub1    This is sub-command 1.
  sub2    This is sub-command 2.
 
This is the foot of the help message.

The same as in argitect(), here the template also allows {{...}} to contain executable code to interpolate and to insert into the template.

sub1_script = system.file("extdata", "sub1.R", package = "argitect")
sub2_script = system.file("extdata", "sub2.R", package = "argitect")
sub_commands(
"This is the head of the help message.

Usage: Rscript main.R [command] [options]

{{ cli_h2('Section') }}
  <sub1={{ sub1_script }}> This is sub-command 1.
  <sub2={{ sub2_script }}> This is sub-command 2.

This is the foot of the help message.

Questions, please contact {{ col_magenta(style_underline(style_italic('your.name@email'))) }}
")
This is the head of the help message. 
 
Usage: Rscript main.R [command] [options] 
 
── Section ── 
  sub1    This is sub-command 1.
  sub2    This is sub-command 2.
 
This is the foot of the help message. 
 
Questions, please contact your.name@email

–-help and –-version

--help on the parent script is the same as giving no argument, which prints the list of sub-commands. --version prints the VERSION variable from the calling environment. Both -h and -v are accepted as well.

VERSION = "1.0.0"
sub_commands(
    "sub1.R", "This is sub command 1.",
    "sub2.R", "This is sub command 2."
)
~\> Rscript main.R --version
1.0.0

Script existence

The sub-scripts must exist. If a specified sub-script path does not exist, sub_commands() raises an error:

sub_commands(
    "sub1", "non_existing_dir/sub1.R", "This is sub command 1."
)
Error:
! Script path(s) do not exist: non_existing_dir/sub1.R.
